headline: An attack ad used her mother. Vance: stop whining.
summary: Vivek Ramaswamy's campaign for Ohio governor made an ad in which Amy Acton's estranged mother calls her a liar, and will spend $4 million to air it. Court records show Acton was 12 when her stepfather was charged with raping her. She has not seen her mother since 1978. Both parties condemned it. Vance said Republicans should stop whining.

cover_question.q: Why is her mum being mean to her?

cover_answer: They haven't spoken since Amy was 12. For a reason.
table_question: Is someone's family fair game in a fight?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Two people want to be the boss of Ohio, and one put the other one's mum on TV saying unkind things about her, in an ad as long as putting on both shoes and a coat. They haven't seen each other since the daughter was 12, because that home wasn't safe for her. Grown-ups on both teams said the ad was wrong, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Only if they hear it. A home that wasn't safe, then the grown-ups.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, and here it is a mum being unkind on TV, which is frightening on its own. So the script says why without saying what: that home wasn't safe, and grown-ups moved her out. Expect "would you ever say that about me?" No. Say it straight, and that both teams called the ad wrong.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Ramaswamy and Acton want to be governor of Ohio. His ad has her own mother calling her a liar. It leaves out why they haven't spoken since 1978: Acton was taken from that home at 12 because her stepfather was charged with hurting her. Every fight has a line, and both teams said this crossed it.
8-12.why: Ad, missing fact, line. Kids this age police lines.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out what's fair and whether adults hold their own side to it, so the script hands them a chain: an ad, the fact it leaves out, and a line people on both teams said was crossed. The line in a fight is the mechanism; they know it from the playground. Expect "is the ad allowed?" Yes. Legal and fair are different things.

13-17.script: Is anything off limits in a campaign? Ramaswamy's ad has Acton's estranged mother calling her a liar. Court records say she was 12 when her stepfather was charged with raping her. The ad tested well, so it gets $4 million. Second: Vance says stop whining. If a line moves with the polling, is it a line?
13-17.why: Off limits, then the line that moves.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: the ad is legal and tested well, and the people who know the story best, in both parties, called it a low. The script asks whether a line that moves with the polling is a line at all, and lets them argue either side. Expect "would it work on you?" Say honestly whether it would, and why.

5-7.q: Why is her mum being mean to her?
5-7.a: Some grown-ups fall out with their parents. Amy was moved out of that home at 12 because it wasn't safe.

8-12.a: Yes. No rule stops it. People in both parties called it wrong anyway.

8-12.q: Why does her mum say she's lying?
8-12.a: Not said. Acton says her mother sided with the man who hurt her.

13-17.q: Does this kind of ad work?
13-17.a: His campaign says it tested well. One professor expects a backfire.
He said politics is a tough business and he cares who governs.
